Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3147); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite:--Joatham.
BiblicalUsage: Joatham is the Greek form of Jotham, the king of Judah, and Matthew names him twice in one verse. In Matthew 1:9 Ozias begat Joatham, and Joatham begat Achaz, and Achaz begat Ezekias, in the line that runs from Abraham to Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Joatham's two mentions in a single verse are the point: a king who did right, named once as a son and once as a father, in the line God kept.
RelatedPeople: Jotham, King of Judah; Ahaz, Son of Jotham
